notes_for_implementers: Read docs/DESIGN.md §3 for the exact signature of anything you call; §5 for every column; docs/MODULES.md for your module's brief. The subsection for each module is named in MODULES.md.

Same-wave modules never import each other; tests/unit/test_wave_imports.py (wave 0) fails your build on the first violation and lint-imports enforces the same layers in CI from wave 5. Upward references go through the Protocols in nour/core/contracts.py (NotifierLike, FreezeLike, AuthFailureSink, IncidentSink, CriticLike, RedactorLike, AuditSink, CounterpartLookup) or injected callables (ApprovalsQueue receives mint; the gate reaches tool handlers via ToolRegistry).

Every side-effecting port method takes a PortCall first; the PortCall comes from AuditLog.span's opened row (ExecContext.call). A port call without an audit id is a type error and CallLog.without_audit() must stay empty.

Every text written into a prompt, memory, audit, owner message, outbound message, handoff or vector index is a SafeStr from LeakGuard.safe()/redact(); observed text shown to the model uses redact (never blocks), text Nour writes uses safe (raises). Never construct SafeStr directly.
Timestamps come only from the injected Clock (DB defaults call clock.process_now()); ids only from IdGenerator; datetime.now( is allowed only in nour/core/clock.py (ruff DTZ + AST walls test).

Nothing the model emits lowers a tier: TierResolver recomputes high_impact, new_counterpart, in_owner_name, irreversible, outbound and data_tier from ToolSpec, config and CRM/beneficiary lookups; tier and data_tier_touched from the model are stored only as model_claimed_*.

The passphrase is extracted, verified and redacted in the ingress process (IngressRedactor) before any row is written; no table ever holds it; LeakGuard.register_plaintext_once makes it a fingerprint hit anywhere. Freeze HIGH_IMPACT and alert the second channel on the FIRST wrong attempt.
The one-way gate carries Tier0Ref references (knowledge-pack keys, Operator-partition contacts, config paths, Operator tasks), never free-text facts; gate_handoff starts at tier K.

Wave 0 (core) is deliberately above the size band (~2,750 lines); split its sitting into types/contracts/ports then config/db/conftest if needed. Every other module is within ~800–1,350 lines including tests.

Config lives in the existing config/ directory (not configs/); the loader is tested against the real files. New files core must add: config/models.yaml, config/capabilities.yaml, config/coats/buzz-avenue.tone.md, config/coats/buzz-avenue.knowledge.md, .env.example, .github/workflows/ci.yml (with a postgres job running the DB tests marked @postgres).

Harness.build defaults: Monday 2026-10-05 07:00 Asia/Dubai, owner +971500000001, passphrase correct-horse-battery, second channel owner@example.com, a canary IBAN planted in the vault. Use tick=True only in the single @wallclock kill-switch test; the 48-hour gate run uses dry_run=True so zero sends is itself an assertion.

Docs/DESIGN.md §7 is the contract for the acceptance module: each §16 criterion and §18 scenario maps to a named file and assertion list; do not weaken an assertion to make a test pass — fix the module it exposes.
